assertions.new_codes_expect: Foreign Transaction Fee: If you make a transaction in a foreign currency, a purchase outside of the United States, or a transaction that is processed outside of the United States (including, for example, online purchases from a merchant located outside of the U.S.), we will charge a foreign transaction fee of {foreign_transaction_fee}% of the transaction amount in U.S. dollars. The foreign transaction fee will be added to the transaction amount and will be included in your Account balance. Should an original foreign transaction be reversed or returned, the associated foreign transaction fee shall be refunded and no further foreign transaction fees will be levied for that specific return.

assertions.new_codes_expect_literal: Foreign Transaction Fee: If you make a transaction in a foreign currency, a purchase outside of the United States, or a transaction that is processed outside of the United States (including, for example, online purchases from a merchant located outside of the U.S.), we will charge a foreign transaction fee of 3% of the transaction amount in U.S. dollars. The foreign transaction fee will be added to the transaction amount and will be included in your Account balance. Should an original foreign transaction be reversed or returned, the associated foreign transaction fee shall be refunded and no further foreign transaction fees will be levied for that specific return.

assertions.new_codes_expect: Foreign Transactions: Transactions in a foreign currency are converted to U.S. dollars by our network providers (Visa and MasterCard) using their procedures in effect at the time the transaction is processed. Currently, they use a government-mandated or wholesale rate. These procedures may change without notice. The conversion rate you get may differ from the rate on the transaction or post date, and from the rate our network provider gets. Any conversion rate costs resulting from our network provider’s procedures will be reflected in the transaction amount posted to your Account. A merchant or other third party may convert a transaction into U.S. dollars or another currency, using a rate they select, before sending it to our network provider.
